rubric.rubric_intent: Determine whether hermes-rubric enforces evidence-first, hedge-disciplined, non-fluency-biased scoring in practice, not just in its README.

dimensions.name: Evidence-gate enforcement in code
dimensions.description: Measures whether the scoring pipeline actually blocks/penalizes scores that lack cited evidence (file:line or quoted passage), rather than just requesting it in the prompt.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Open src/ and locate the scoring stage. Look for explicit checks that reject or hedge dimensions with empty/unverifiable evidence fields (e.g. regex for file:line, quote-in-source checks, or a branch that flips hedge=true when evidence is missing). Quote the exact function and lines. If the only 'enforcement' is a prompt string telling the LLM to cite, that is weak evidence.

dimensions.name: Adversarial dimension synthesis
dimensions.description: Measures whether the rubric-synthesis stage produces dimensions capable of sinking the target, not just flattering ones — including an explicit mechanism to require or reward adversarial cuts.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Inspect the synthesis prompt(s) and any synthesis tests in tests/ or calibration/. Quote the lines that instruct the model to include dimensions that could *fail* the target. Check calibration/ for stored rubrics on prior targets and count how many dimensions were plausibly target-sinking versus friendly restatements. Report ratio.

dimensions.name: Hedging discipline (explicit hedge flag, not score shading)
dimensions.description: Measures whether thin-evidence cases are surfaced via an explicit hedge=true flag rather than silently compressed toward the mean.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Grep src/ and tests/ for 'hedge'. Confirm the output schema carries a per-dimension hedge boolean and that the scoring logic sets it when evidence quality is low (not when score is low). Check applied/ outputs for real runs: do low-evidence dims actually ship with hedge=true, or are scores just nudged? Quote at least one run.

dimensions.name: Fluency-bias resistance (adversarial test presence)
dimensions.description: Measures whether the repo contains a test that compares a terse-substantive target against a polished-hollow one and asserts the substantive one wins.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Search tests/ for fixtures pairing 'hollow' / 'marketing' / 'polished' vs 'terse' / 'substantive' / 'sparse'. Quote the assertion. If no such adversarial pair exists, the claim is unverified — score low and do not hedge upward on absence.

dimensions.name: Receipt / reproducibility manifest
dimensions.description: Measures whether each score run emits a hash or manifest (inputs, model, prompt version, rubric) that lets a third party re-run and diff.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Inspect the output schema and any --out artifacts in applied/. Confirm presence of: input hash, rubric hash, backend/model identifier, prompt/version string. Absence of any one of these lowers the score. Quote the manifest fields from a real output file.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring non-rubber-stamp
dimensions.description: Measures whether, when pointed at itself, hermes-rubric has produced (or is structurally capable of producing) dimensions that score itself below ceiling on at least one non-trivial axis.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Check applied/ for any self-run artifacts. If present, list dimensions scored below max and confirm the evidence is drawn from code, not README paraphrase. If no self-run exists, hedge=true and note the absence rather than assuming pass or fail.

dimensions.name: Bounded LLM surface (LLM does not author the claims being judged)
dimensions.description: Measures whether the pipeline uses the LLM only for synthesis / evidence extraction / scoring, and never lets the LLM invent target content that then gets scored.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Trace the data flow in src/: the 'target' input must be read verbatim from disk and passed as context, not summarized or rewritten by the LLM before scoring. Quote the function that loads the target and confirm no LLM call sits between load and evidence collection.

dimensions.name: Evidence-source discrimination (code vs README-marketing)
dimensions.description: Measures whether collected evidence is preferentially drawn from source/tests rather than the target's own README/marketing copy when both are available.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: In any applied/ run on a repo target, tally evidence citations by file type: src/tests vs README/docs. A tool that mostly cites README back at itself is rubber-stamping. Report the ratio; quote 2-3 example citations.

evidence_citations.evidence_summary: score.py:56-64 enforces gates in code after the LLM returns: hedged dimensions are clamped to [3,7] and dimensions with evidence_found=false are capped at 3, with rationale annotation. Enforcement is deterministic and not reliant on the prompt. Caveat: the gate reads flag fields (ev['hedge'], ev['evidence_found']) set during evidence collection rather than re-validating the citation format (e.g. regex for file:line or quote-in-source), so the code trusts the evidence stage's self-report.

citations.quote: Dimensions must be DISCRIMINATING: a weak and strong target must score differently. If two targets would always get the same score, drop that dimension.
Do NOT invent dimensions for things you cannot observe in the target.
Given two targets of known different quality, the rubric produces detectably different scores. A rubric that scores everything 6-8 regardless of quality has zero discrimination power.
FM-06 (Fluency inflation — rubrics that don't discriminate reward surface polish), FM-19 (Boilerplate dimensions are non-discriminating by construction)
Apply the META-RUBRIC when evaluating the quality of a synthesized rubric (Stage 1 output) before trusting its Stage 3 scores.
No stored synthesized rubrics in calibration/dataset.jsonl — keys are id, domain, intent, context, target, target_name, human_score, notes. No 'dimensions' field present in any of 15 rows.
tests/test_synthesize.py contains 3 tests (valid rubric, min-dimensions validation, JSON extraction) — none assert that synthesized dimensions include target-sinking cuts.

evidence_citations.evidence_summary: The synthesis prompt enforces discrimination ('a weak and strong target must score differently') and forbids unobservable dimensions, which indirectly pushes toward target-sinking capacity. A separate META-RUBRIC evaluates Discrimination Power post-hoc and is motivated by fluency-inflation / boilerplate failure modes. However, there is NO explicit instruction in the synthesis prompt to include dimensions that could fail the target, no reward for adversarial cuts, and no stored rubrics in calibration/dataset.jsonl to compute a sinking-vs-friendly ratio (dataset rows contain only human_score, not synthesized dimensions). Adversarial intent is present in the meta-evaluation layer but not wired into synthesis itself.

evidence_citations.evidence_summary: read_target() loads the target verbatim from disk via p.read_text() (or concatenates raw file contents for directories) and returns the string unchanged. cli.py passes this string directly into collect_evidence, which forwards it to _collect_one where it is only truncated (sliced), never LLM-rewritten, before being used as context for evidence extraction. No LLM call sits between load and evidence collection.
